title: Initial face and final edge admit a finite inner-horn filtration
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and inner horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and colimits of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a subset $S\subseteq[n]$, let $\Delta^S\subseteq\Delta^n$ consist of the monotone maps with image contained in $S$. For every integer $n>0$, put $T=\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}$, $I=\Delta^{\{n-1,n\}}$, and $K=T\cup I\subseteq\Delta^n$. There is a finite filtration $K=K_0\subseteq K_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq K_N=\Delta^n$ in which every $K_{j-1}\hookrightarrow K_j$ is a pushout of an inner horn inclusion $\Lambda^{d_j}_{a_j}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{d_j}$, with $d_j\geq2$ and $0<a_j<d_j$. Each pushout is computed degreewise in sets. The case $n=1$ permits $N=0$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp.182–183, the initial-face/final-edge replacement implicit in the second pushout diagram; finite horn-filtration formulation extracted by agent. Read online 2026-10-17. WANTED: archival copy under literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result.

proof.text: By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], an $r$-simplex of $\Delta^n$ is a monotone map $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$, with operators given by precomposition. For every vertex set $V$, membership in $\Delta^V$ means $\operatorname{im}(\alpha)\subseteq V$. Thus unions of these faces are simplicial subsets and their membership is tested in every degree by the image set. In particular $\alpha\in K$ if and only if $n\notin\operatorname{im}(\alpha)$ or $\operatorname{im}(\alpha)\subseteq\{n-1,n\}$. This criterion includes degenerate simplices.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp.182–183 (PDF pages 199–200); direct image-set expansion of the initial-face/final-edge inclusion used in the second pushout diagram. Online source read 2026-10-17; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: For $n=1$, the final edge $I$ is already $\Delta^1$, so $K=\Delta^1$ and take $N=0$. Assume henceforth $n\geq2$. Let $P$ be the collection of vertex sets $V\subseteq[n]$ containing $\{n-1,n\}$ and at least one element of $\{0,\ldots,n-2\}$. This is a finite collection. Enumerate its distinct members $V_1,\ldots,V_N$ in increasing cardinality, choosing any order within a cardinality. Define $K_0=K$ and $K_j=K\cup\bigcup_{b\leq j}\Delta^{V_b}$. These are increasing simplicial subsets by Step 1. The full vertex set $[n]$ is the unique largest member of $P$, so $V_N=[n]$ and $K_N=\Delta^n$.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp.182–183 (PDF pages 199–200); direct image-set expansion of the initial-face/final-edge inclusion used in the second pushout diagram. Online source read 2026-10-17; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: At stage $j$, write $V=V_j=\{v_0<\cdots<v_d\}$ and let $a$ be the index of $n-1$. The last vertex is $n$, and there is an earlier vertex less than $n-1$, so $d\geq2$ and $0<a<d$ (indeed $a=d-1$). For each $v\in V\setminus\{n-1\}$, the face $\Delta^{V\setminus\{v\}}$ lies in $K_{j-1}$. If $v=n$, it lies in the initial face $T$. If $v<n-1$ and it is the sole earlier vertex of $V$, the remaining face is $I$. Otherwise $V\setminus\{v\}$ belongs to $P$ and has smaller cardinality, so it occurred earlier. Thus all codimension-one faces except possibly the $a$th are present.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp.182–183 (PDF pages 199–200); direct image-set expansion of the initial-face/final-edge inclusion used in the second pushout diagram. Online source read 2026-10-17; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Put $F=V\setminus\{n-1\}$. Neither the simplex on $F$ nor the simplex on $V$ is in $K_{j-1}$. For $F$, the criterion of Step 1 excludes membership in $K$: it contains $n$ and a vertex less than $n-1$. If $F$ were contained in an earlier $V_b$, then $n-1\in V_b$ gives $V=F\cup\{n-1\}\subseteq V_b$. But $b<j$ gives $|V_b|\leq|V|$, forcing $V_b=V$, contrary to distinctness. The same argument, or restriction to the face $F$, excludes the simplex on $V$. More generally no simplex whose image is $F$ or $V$ is present: membership in any part of the defining union requires that entire image be contained in its vertex set.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp.182–183 (PDF pages 199–200); direct image-set expansion of the initial-face/final-edge inclusion used in the second pushout diagram. Online source read 2026-10-17; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: Use the increasing bijection $[d]\to V$ to identify $\Delta^d$ with $\Delta^V$. Its inverse image of $K_{j-1}$ is exactly $\Lambda_a^d$. Indeed the horn definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] says that its simplices omit some vertex of $V$ other than $n-1$; such simplices lie in one of the faces present by Step 3. Conversely, if a simplex omits no vertex other than possibly $n-1$, its image is $F$ or $V$, which Step 4 excludes. This is an equality in every degree, including degeneracies, and the identification commutes with precomposition. Step 3 verified that this horn is inner.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp.182–183 (PDF pages 199–200); direct image-set expansion of the initial-face/final-edge inclusion used in the second pushout diagram. Online source read 2026-10-17; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: We have $K_j=K_{j-1}\cup\Delta^V$ and, by Step 5, the intersection is the image of $\Lambda_a^d$. The square of these inclusions is a degreewise pushout in sets: its set pushout identifies precisely the two copies of their intersection, and its image is precisely the union, without further identifications. Equivalently maps from the two parts agreeing on the horn glue uniquely by using the specified map on each part. Precomposition preserves both parts and their intersection, so gluing simplicial maps gives a simplicial map. This proves the pushout universal property of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] in simplicial sets as well. Thus each stage is the required inner horn pushout, with $d_j=d$ and $a_j=a$. Together with Step 2 this is the asserted finite filtration.
